classification.difficultyReason: Rearrange the arc-length formula to find a radius or an angle in radians.

content.prompt: Find the value of the unknown side or angle in the following.

spec.sourceRegion: Essential Problems 9, bottom of left column
spec.description: Unshaded sector opening upward, with a black centre dot, the arc label above the boundary and the radius label outside the right radius.
spec.mathematics: The arc length is 4π, the central angle is π/3 radians and the radius r is unknown. No length unit is printed.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the unknown r are visible.

spec.sourceRegion: Essential Problems 10, bottom of left column
spec.description: Broad unshaded sector opening upward, with an arc label above the boundary, an interior angle marker and a black centre dot.
spec.mathematics: The arc length is 5π and the radius is 6. The central angle θ is unknown. The construction is consistent with these givens without printing its angular value.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the arc length, radius and unknown θ are visible.

spec.sourceRegion: Essential Problems 11, top of right column
spec.description: Nearly semicircular unshaded sector above a black centre dot. The two radii are slightly inclined and are not collinear. There is no straight-angle symbol.
spec.mathematics: The arc length is 15, the radius is 5 and θ is unknown. Internal geometry is derived from the printed givens; no additional angular datum is displayed.
spec.answerVisibility: The unknown θ remains symbolic. Its numerical value is absent from the student diagram.

spec.sourceRegion: Essential Problems 12, top of right column
spec.description: Unshaded major sector with a lower wedge missing, a black centre dot and a reflex angle marker passing through the retained upper region.
spec.mathematics: The major arc has length 8 and subtends 4π/3 radians. The radius r is unknown. The reflex marker follows the major sector rather than the missing wedge.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied arc length, reflex angle and unknown r are visible.

answer.worked:
Use $l=r\theta$ with the labelled major-sector angle:
$$\begin{align*}r&=\frac{l}{\theta}\\r&=\frac{8}{4\pi/3}\\r&=\frac{6}{\pi}.\end{align*}$$
